recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.

A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Cards as a Daily Mirror", "body": "Michael Wann opens with the habit that frames the whole conversation: each morning he draws from the Yijing, the tarot and one looser contemporary deck, logs the results in a calendar built on new moon to new moon cycles, and later checks which cards came up most against how the month actually felt. He says the practice adds mystery in a tangible, playable way. Then he and Chance draw Yijing cards live, Chance with Taming Power of the Small and Michael with Great Power, and Chance calls the pairing mind blowing given how often he consults the deck."}, {"title": "Defining Words Before Debating Them", "body": "Michael insists on asking how someone defines a word before building on it, so that neither side assumes it knows what the other means. Chance backs this with Confucius, arguing that without shared meanings nothing gets done, and says he likes old dictionaries such as Webster's 1828, where, he says, race meant family and he sees signs of a PR campaign to change a word's reputation. Their riff on the rat race, rats and vultures turns a reputation for filth into a case for reclaiming symbols, with Michael wanting to take back the rat."}, {"title": "Inventing Your Own System", "body": "Michael describes how he began making collages from cut paper around 2010 because he wanted the images out of his head without learning to paint or studying under anyone. Inventing his own system, he says, gave him freedom, since there was no outside standard to be wrong against, and he sits with each piece until the next step arrives. Chance adds that the creative person simply picks a step while the non-creative person freezes, ties it to verbs over nouns in a Tao based life, and credits his own podcast templates for his efficiency and confidence."}, {"title": "The Tao Through a Money Book", "body": "Michael recalls a yin and yang symbol on a skateboard shirt from his childhood, then a stretch in his late twenties as a product manager when he studied personal finance intently. Hunting in a library for The Richest Man in Babylon, he found The Tao of Money on the shelf beside it, felt what he calls a tuning fork moment inside, and says it became his threshold into the Tao Te Ching and the Yijing. Chance suggests fate served him better than Babylon would have, noting that money and Tao are both conceptualized as flow and current."}, {"title": "Money, Currency and Cash Flow", "body": "Michael argues that Occam's razor suits the natural world but fails against human schemes, and that a debt based central banking system was designed so its debts cannot be repaid, which he calls a mathematical impossibility. Separating money from currency, he treats currency as cash flow that must keep moving, and says hoarding out of fear of never having enough blocks it. Chance adds that treating money as evil builds its own barrier, and offers his definitions: currency as a medium of exchange, money as a store of value, and wealth as tangible things that bring prosperity."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: The syncromystic sage of the Susquehanna returns! Michael Wann is a multi-disciplinary creator and reality-analyst. In this episode we talk about I Ching, initiating the synchronicity flow state, the Tao of money, and much more.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Innocence, Passes and Human Drives", "body": "Back from the break, Chance shows the Innocence card he pulled while waiting, calling it the inversion of Great Power, built from the same elements flipped, and noting that 34 and 25 each reduce to seven. Michael says the swing from Taming Power of the Small to Great Power felt less like a slam dunk than a beautiful pass you do not see coming. He then grounds his ideas in the body, which he takes literally as a macrocosm, and sorts human drives by strength, from breathing and expulsion down to hunger and thirst, with Chance noting the body wants you to keep functioning."}, {"title": "The Internet, Pornography and the Hex Idea", "body": "Chance cites the internet maxim Rule 34 and speculates that pop culture's sexual imagery may be a kind of hex, meant to get young minds identified with the image of sex. Michael traces the internet to the military industrial complex, saying ARPANET's architect held a post in behavioral sciences at the Department of Defense, and describes everyone being born into a pornographic world. He relays Alan Watt's claim that Roman and Greek art carried sexual imagery, which he admits he has not verified, and asks how people might reclaim a culture already shaped by it."}, {"title": "Art, Artificiality and Tao", "body": "Chance proposes that if satanic means adversarial to Tao, the word points at artificiality, and says one English word covers two opposite ideas: healing arts like tai chi on one side, jargon and legalese on the other. Michael asks how art should be defined, and they settle on art as a verb, a process flowing from the imagination. Michael adds that artificial blends art with official, a hint that the choice ahead is whether to walk the official path. Chance argues artifice itself is two sided, either in sync with nature or dissonant with it."}, {"title": "Stories, Mystery and the Threshold", "body": "Chance says he cannot simply believe stories that are not grounded in his own reality, such as claims about a Galactic Federation, and borrows the term mysteria for being trapped in someone else's idea about an idea. Michael agrees and describes his own stance: come as far as he can toward what he knows, accept that life is a mysterious experience, then jump from that threshold into whichever story helps, staying honest that he could deconstruct it. He admires people who say plainly what they choose to believe and why."}, {"title": "Sacred Objects and Handmade Symbols", "body": "Michael shows a leather bag and wand he made, explaining how a remark about a museum quality walking stick led him to a sand and glue technique and then to sacred objects, with about a month of detail work in the bag. The wand pairs Himalayan quartz with tektite and carries phallic and yoni symbolism, offered as a counterpoint to the pornography discussed earlier. Chance calls it heirloom quality, something a descendant might revere, and Michael presents it as a permission slip for others to invent their own work, imagining workshops where people build symbolic forms."}]

fields.Plus Quotes JSON: [{"text": "A pass you did not see coming, that to me is the most beautiful thing in any sport.", "author": "Michael Wann", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/b7e0ef5f-142f-46eb-a25f-b387285ea071/MICHAEL-WANN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The human body is a macrocosm of everything, and I take that very, very literally.", "author": "Michael Wann", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/b7e0ef5f-142f-46eb-a25f-b387285ea071/MICHAEL-WANN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Art itself is not the evil, is not the disempowering thing.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Most people are trapped within words, trapped within the idea about an idea that was someone else's idea. And what I mean by that is we're not going to know.", "author": "Michael Wann", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/b7e0ef5f-142f-46eb-a25f-b387285ea071/MICHAEL-WANN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I'm not trying to control anyone, but there is a power when you can paint pictures in people's minds.", "author": "Michael Wann", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/b7e0ef5f-142f-46eb-a25f-b387285ea071/MICHAEL-WANN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Anything can be sacred, and it's really the approach you take to it.", "author": "Michael Wann", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/b7e0ef5f-142f-46eb-a25f-b387285ea071/MICHAEL-WANN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "You can just do it the way you would do it, and that's going to be the most authentic way.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "I try to bring a lot of these kind of conceptual ideas. I'm always trying to ground it into something which is more tangible, which we can understand.", "author": "Michael Wann", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/b7e0ef5f-142f-46eb-a25f-b387285ea071/MICHAEL-WANN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "There's something really, really enticing and magical about that connection between men and women when there's a mystery tied into it.", "author": "Michael Wann", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/b7e0ef5f-142f-46eb-a25f-b387285ea071/MICHAEL-WANN.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}]
